Keep custom properties and extension groups the same on your devices.

A device can receive another device's definitions, or two devices can keep each other in step. Each device applies what it receives to its own database. Safe changes apply by themselves; conflicts, deletions of things in use and type changes wait for you, and deciding on one device closes the same question on the others. Library content never travels.

You built 100 properties on the desktop. On the laptop you turn on definitions sharing, then on the desktop's Device map you choose “Keep in step both ways” with the laptop, approve on the laptop, and link the six it already had. From then on a tag you add on either computer shows up on the other.
helpCenter.dataSync.headline: Keep your structure the same on every device
helpCenter.dataSync.intro: Each device keeps its own library, but the structure you build to organize it — custom properties with their choices, tags and levels, and extension groups — can stay the same on all your devices. One device can receive another's changes, or both can keep each other in step. Nothing in your library travels: no resources, no values, no files.
helpCenter.dataSync.how.title: How data sync works
helpCenter.dataSync.how.link.title: Link
helpCenter.dataSync.how.link.desc: First, on the other device, open Data sync → This device and turn on “Let devices I approve read this device's definitions” (if remote access is off there, this turns it on, with pairing required). Then, on the Device map, choose “Receive only” or “Keep in step both ways” on the line to that device, and approve once on it.
helpCenter.dataSync.how.link.descNoMap: First, on the other device, open Data sync → This device and turn on sharing (if remote access is off there, this turns it on, with pairing required). Then, in System → Data sync, choose “Sync with another device”, and approve once on that device.
helpCenter.dataSync.how.review.title: First sync
helpCenter.dataSync.how.review.desc: The device that starts the link sees a preview first: what the first sync will create and update on it, and what it will ask you about. Leave out any definition you want, then press Start. A definition with the same name is never linked by itself: after the start it waits in Needs you, where you link the two or keep both. The other device waits until that is settled, then applies only safe changes and asks you about everything else.
helpCenter.dataSync.how.inStep.title: In step
helpCenter.dataSync.how.inStep.desc: Afterwards, changes arrive within a minute or two while both devices are on. Safe changes apply by themselves, and the history lists them.
helpCenter.dataSync.how.needsYou.title: Needs you
helpCenter.dataSync.how.needsYou.desc: When both devices changed the same thing differently, when something in use was deleted, or when a type changed, it waits for you in Data sync → Needs you.
helpCenter.dataSync.modes.title: Ways to sync with a device
helpCenter.dataSync.modes.follow.title: Receive only
helpCenter.dataSync.modes.follow.desc: This device takes the other device's definitions and keeps its own additions. When both changed the same thing, the other device's version wins — unless the value here came from a third device; then it waits for you.
helpCenter.dataSync.modes.twoWay.title: Keep in step both ways
helpCenter.dataSync.modes.twoWay.desc: Each device receives the other's definitions and combines them field by field. When both changed the same thing differently, it waits for you on both.
helpCenter.dataSync.modes.loops: Two devices that each receive only from the other work as keeping in step both ways. Longer loops — one device receiving from a second, the second from a third and the third from the first — are not supported, because changes could go round in circles: keep such devices in step both ways instead.
helpCenter.dataSync.modes.caption: Arrows point to the receiving device and use the source device’s color. If you only need one synchronization, check that it has completed and then turn off that device’s sync. Data already synchronized stays here.
helpCenter.dataSync.types.title: What data sync keeps in step today
helpCenter.dataSync.types.travels: Kept in step between your devices
helpCenter.dataSync.types.customProperty: Name, type, settings and order, with the options of single and multiple choice properties, tags with their groups, multilevel options, and their colors. A property can be set to sync its definition only, on every device at once.
helpCenter.dataSync.types.extensionGroup: The name of each group and the file extensions in it.
helpCenter.dataSync.types.more: Other kinds of definitions are not synced yet.
helpCenter.dataSync.never.title: Never synced
helpCenter.dataSync.never.desc: Each device keeps these to itself.
helpCenter.dataSync.never.library: Resources, property values, covers and play history
helpCenter.dataSync.never.paths: Folders, paths, path marks and media library settings
helpCenter.dataSync.never.secrets: Accounts, cookies, passwords and API keys
helpCenter.dataSync.never.settings: App settings and this device's identity
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.title: When two devices change the same thing
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.step.renam: {{here}} renames the property Artist to Artists, and {{there}} renames it to Performer.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.step.ask: {{here}} and {{there}} both ask you, under Needs you, which name to keep.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.step.decid: You keep Performer on {{there}}. The question on {{here}} closes by itself and says it was resolved on {{there}}.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.fields: Different changes to one definition — one device renames it, the other adds an option — are simply combined.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.same: The same thing changed differently on both devices waits in Needs you on both, and the other device's other changes to that definition wait with it until you decide. Decide on either one; the other closes by itself and says where it was decided.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.hub: A device that is always on, such as a NAS, passes changes between computers that are rarely on together. Questions you also get on a computer close on the NAS as soon as you answer them there. Questions only the NAS has wait on the NAS: your computers show “NAS has N changes waiting for a decision”, and until you decide there — by switching the window to it — those changes do not reach the other computers.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.types: A type change always asks first and shows how the values here would change.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.case: When a property ignores case, options that differ only in case are the same option, so renaming one only in case stays on this device.
helpCenter.dataSync.conflicts.labelWrite: Path marks and workflows that set an option by its name can bring back an old name after the option was renamed on another device; the recreated option is then synced like any new one.
helpCenter.dataSync.deletes.title: When something is deleted
helpCenter.dataSync.deletes.options: An option deleted on the other device is removed here too when no resource here uses it and it was not changed here since; one you renamed, recolored or moved here is kept and offered back to the other device. When many options of one property are removed at once, sync asks first. One that resources here still use is kept until you decide: remove it here too, keep it only on this device, or, when the two keep in step both ways, bring it back everywhere.
helpCenter.dataSync.deletes.definitions: Sync deletes a whole definition by itself only when sync created it here, nothing changed it here since, and it has no values. Any other deletion waits for you, and so does every deletion of a type when the other device deletes many of them at once; when a deletion would remove values here, the database is backed up first by default.
helpCenter.dataSync.deletes.edited: When two devices keep in step both ways, a definition changed on one after the other deleted it is kept where it was changed, and the device that deleted it asks whether to bring it back. A device that only receives from the one that deleted it asks instead whether to delete it here too.
helpCenter.dataSync.deletes.filters: Saved filters that used a removed option lose that condition.
helpCenter.dataSync.recover.title: History, pauses and restores
helpCenter.dataSync.pause.title: When sync pauses by itself
helpCenter.dataSync.pause.desc: Sync with a device pauses, and says why, when that device looks reset or restored from a backup. You can resume or stop syncing.
helpCenter.dataSync.restore.title: After restoring a backup
helpCenter.dataSync.restore.desc: If this device's data goes back in time — restored from a backup, or copied from another computer — sync notices, from its own records or from what your other devices have seen, and pauses. Data sync then asks what wins: this device's definitions or the other devices'. Until you choose, the paused sync waits, so older definitions never overwrite newer ones.
helpCenter.dataSync.safety.title: What data sync never does
helpCenter.dataSync.safety.noValues: It never changes your resources' values by itself.
helpCenter.dataSync.safety.noMerge: It never merges two definitions just because they have the same name.
helpCenter.dataSync.safety.noRemote: Another device can only read definitions. This device applies every change and records it in the sync history.
helpCenter.dataSync.safety.stop: Stopping sync keeps everything you have.
helpCenter.dataSync.safety.grant: Only this device, or a device paired with it, can let another device read its definitions.
helpCenter.dataSync.where.title: Where to find it
helpCenter.dataSync.where.map: On the Device map, the data sync line between two devices shows what is synced; its arrow points to the device that receives. Select it to change it.
helpCenter.dataSync.where.page: System → Data sync lists what needs you, requests and the history. It also works in a window switched to another device.
helpCenter.dataSync.where.nas: A NAS has no screen: switch the window to it and use Data sync there, or, inside its container, list requests with federation datasync requests and approve one with federation datasync approve. With BAKABASE_DATASYNC_SHARING=true, sharing is turned on again at every start. The NAS must run the same data sync version as your other devices: when you update them, update it too.
helpCenter.dataSync.vsOthers: Device management lets you search, view and manage resources from added devices here. Data sync keeps definitions such as custom properties and media libraries consistent, so each device organizes resources the same way.
helpCenter.dataSync.how.history.title: Review the history
helpCenter.dataSync.how.history.desc: History records completed changes for review. To make a correction, edit the data on its page and sync again. History keeps the last 30 days and at least the newest 500 entries, within a 64 MB limit.
helpCenter.dataSync.history.title: Correcting synced data
helpCenter.dataSync.history.desc: Edit a custom property or extension group on its usual page, then sync again. Resolve any conflicts against the current data. Syncing does not automatically restore a historical version or recover deleted property values. To restore a database backup, quit Bakabase first, then replace the database with that backup.
